look_here_first: Look closely at the pad areoles: many dense rust-red to reddish-brown glochid clusters, with ordinary long rigid spines typically absent. Then check the whole branching pad habit; do not use pad color or the red dots alone.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Flattened jointed cactus pads with regular areoles

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Dense reddish-brown to rusty glochid tufts at the areoles

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Ordinary long stiff spines often absent; inspect multiple mature pads

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Branching clump of pad segments; pad habit alone is insufficient

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Flowers and fruit should be checked when present, but areole/spine structure is the first useful cue

lookalikes.differences: Distinguish from O. microdasys using expert-confirmed taxon concept, pad/areole distribution, and habitat; its colored glochids alone are not species-proof. Unlike the reviewed strict O. azurea comparison, mature O. rufida usually lacks obvious long rigid spines.
